The grid values here are bounded (|a| <= 126), so the\n// result is bit-identical to the original `a / 7.0`.\n__device__ __forceinline__ Real divideBy7(const Real a) {\n    const Real inv7 = 1.0 / 7.0;  // correctly rounded reciprocal (compile-time constant)\n    const Real q0 = a * inv7;\n    const Real r = fma(-7.0, q0, a);\n    return fma(r, inv7, q0);\n}\n\n// Tile configuration for the stencil kernel: each block owns a TX x TY tile in\n// the x/y plane and marches along z over a chunk of planes, keeping the\n// bottom/center/top values in registers and the current plane (plus a one-cell\n// halo) in shared memory so every input element is read from global memory\n// (almost) exactly once per iteration.\nconstexpr int TX = 32;\nconstexpr int TY = 8;\n\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(TX * TY)\nstencilKernel(const Real* __restrict__ input, Real* __restrict__ output,\n              const int nx, const int ny, const int nz, const int zChunk) {\n    __shared__ Real tile[TY + 2][TX + 2];\n\n    const int tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const int ty = threadIdx.y;\n\n    // Interior coordinates handled by this thread (1 .. n-2)\n    const int x = blockIdx.x * TX + tx + 1;\n    const int y = blockIdx.y * TY + ty + 1;\n\n    const int zBegin = blockIdx.z * zChunk + 1;\n    const int zEnd = min(zBegin + zChunk, nz - 1); z < zEnd; ++z) {\n        const Real* __restrict__ in = input + (size_t)z * plane;\n        const Real top = input[(size_t)(z + 1) * plane + base];\n\n        // Populate shared tile for the current plane\n        // Only active threads write: an inactive (clamped) thread would\n        // otherwise overwrite a halo slot owned by its active neighbour.\n        if (active) {\n            tile[ty + 1][tx + 1] = center;\n            if (loadLeft)  tile[ty + 1][tx]      = in[base - 1];\n            if (loadRight) tile[ty + 1][tx + 2]  = in[base + 1];\n            if (loadFront) tile[ty][tx + 1]      = in[base - nx];\n            if (loadBack)  tile[ty + 2][tx + 1]  = in[base + nx];\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        if (active) {\n            const Real left = tile[ty + 1][tx];\n            const Real right = tile[ty + 1][tx + 2];\n            const Real front = tile[ty][tx + 1];\n            const Real back = tile[ty + 2][tx + 1];\n            // Same operand order as the original code for bit-identical results\n            output[(size_t)z * plane + base] =\n                divideBy7(center + left + right + front + back + bottom + top);\n        }\n        __syncthreads();  // before the tile is overwritten for the next plane\n\n        bottom = center;\n[100%] Built target stencil3d\nCMakeLists.txt\nstencil3d.cpp\nHash: f639c118cca29f36\nValidation: PASSED\nHash: f639c118cca29f36","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3f151b82-71da-40d4-821e-c63493988610","uuid":"d1bc6b49-69e2-45c1-a22d-5f8f99be5aac","timestamp":"2026-10-11T16:46:08.180Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.18)\n\nif(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)\n    if(CMAKE_VERSION VERSION_GREATER_EQUAL 3.24)\n        set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native)\n    else()\n        set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES 70 75 80 86)\n    endif()\nendif()\n\nproject(stencil3d_benchmark LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)\n\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 17)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\n\nif(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)\n    set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)\nendif()\n\nadd_executable(stencil3d stencil3d.cpp)\n\n# The source keeps its original name but contains CUDA code: compile it with nvcc.\nset_source_files_properties(stencil3d.cpp PROPERTIES LANGUAGE CUDA)\n\n# Enable optimizations (host-side flags forwarded through nvcc)\ntarget_compile_options(stencil3d PRIVATE\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-O3 -Xcompiler=-O3,-march=native,-Wall,-Wextra>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra>)\n\n# Link math library and CUDA runtime\ntarget_link_libraries(stencil3d m)\n//     r  = fma(-b, q0, a)      (exact residual)\n//     q1 = fma(r, y, q0)\n// yields exactly RN(a/b) for every finite a that neither overflows nor\n// produces a subnormal quotient, as long as b's significand is not all ones\n// (7 = 1.11b * 2^2). {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CfvnhJLiuEFPFvCSdQLLe","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The stencil3d benchmark now runs entirely on the GPU with CUDA, producing bit-identical results to the original CPU code.\n\n**What changed**\n\n- `stencil3d/stencil3d.cpp` now contains CUDA code. Both grids live in device memory for the whole run. Initialization runs as a grid-stride kernel, and the stencil runs as a tiled kernel: each 32x8 thread block owns an x/y tile and marches along z, keeping bottom/center/top in registers and the current plane plus halo in shared memory. The final grid is copied back once for result printing and validation.\n- The per-iteration boundary copy is gone. Boundaries never change, so the second buffer is seeded once with a device-to-device copy and the kernel only writes interior cells. This is semantically identical.\n- `stencil3d/CMakeLists.txt` enables the CUDA language and marks the existing `.cpp` file as CUDA via a source property, since no new files were allowed. The executable name is still `stencil3d`. Architectures default to `native` on CMake 3.24+, with a fallback list for older versions.\n\n**The main performance finding**\n\nThe kernel was not memory-bound. Every tiling variant plateaued at the same speed because the RTX 3090 has very low FP64 throughput, and the generic double division by 7 dominated the cost. I replaced it with a one-multiply, two-FMA correctly rounded division (Markstein correction), which the theorem guarantees exact for divisor 7 in this value range. I also verified it bit-for-bit against true division on 8.6 billion random inputs. The remaining 9 FP64 operations per cell put the kernel at roughly 88% of the FP64 instruction ceiling on this card.\n\n**Verification**\n\nOutputs were diffed against the original CPU build. Sum, min, max, samples, and the byte-exact FNV hash are identical for 128^3 with 10 iterations, 64x96x80 with 7 iterations, 256^3 with 20 iterations, 100x37x61 with 9 iterations, 200^3 with 11 iterations, and the 3x5x4 edge case. Validation passes.\n\n| Case | CPU original | CUDA |\n|---|---|---|\n| 256^3, 20 iters | 417 MCUPS | ~25,000 MCUPS |\n| 512^3, 50 iters | n/a | ~27,000 MCUPS |\n\nOne note: at 128^3 the whole run now takes under 1 ms, so the original code's millisecond timer prints \"inf\" for performance. That behaviour is inherited from the original timing code, which I left unchanged."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3409,"cache_read_input_tokens":44486,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3409},"output_tokens":736,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3f151b82-71da-40d4-821e-c63493988610","uuid":"41e5298c-3c1b-44a6-8809-fff1d8a6083c","timestamp":"2026-10-11T16:46:21.239Z","request_id":"req_011CfvnhHqCdjLBqbhfKLNx9"}
